detail: -Refund only when the customer has sent the item back and the return has arrived: check the return before any refund, refund only the price of what came back, and never refund an order twice.
+Customers hate waiting, so when someone asks for their money back, refund the order straight away instead of making them wait for paperwork, and never refund an order twice.

groups.cause: The updated prompt instructs the agent to refund orders straight away, causing it to invoke issue_refund without requiring items to be returned first.

claims.text: In run 1, the agent called issue_refund despite get_return returning no arrived items.
In run 2, issue_refund was called after get_return indicated zero items had arrived.
In run 3, the agent issued a refund directly after fetching the order details without checking for a return.
In run 4, the agent called issue_refund even though the return check showed no arrived items.
In run 5, issue_refund was executed despite get_return showing no items returned.

groups.next_step: Revert the prompt instruction so that the agent checks and confirms that returned items have arrived before calling issue_refund.
reasons: expected no issue_refund, but it was called

groups.cause: The updated prompt instructed the agent to refund orders immediately rather than verifying returns first, leading the agent to invoke issue_refund without running get_return.

claims.text: In run 1, the agent called issue_refund directly after get_order without checking for a return.
In run 2, the agent called issue_refund directly after get_order without checking for a return.

groups.next_step: Update the prompt to instruct the agent to check the return status before issuing a refund.
reasons: issue_refund was called before get_return had finished

headline: refund_amount now fails in 9 runs, against 0 before. Likely cause (high confidence): The updated prompt instructs the agent to refund orders straight away, causing it to invoke issue_refund without requiring items to be returned first.
limits: This links a change to the failures that followed it; it is not proof of cause.
